data.name: Melchizedek
data.gender_notes: Melchizedek is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.short_meaning: King of Salem, priest of God Most High
data.long_meaning: Melchizedek, a name of Hebrew origin, means 'King of Righteousness, or King of Salem, priest of God Most High'. In the Bible, he is a figure of great importance in Jewish and Christian tradition, recognized as a priest and king who offered a sacrifice and blessed Abram, the future father of the Israelites. The name Melchizedek carries the meaning “King of Salem, priest of God Most High” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Melchizedek usually hope their child will grow to embody king of salem, priest of god most high and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of divine priesthood, unity of sacred and secular powers
data.etymology: Melchizedek belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “King of Salem, priest of God Most High.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Melchizedek total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

in_hebrew.name: מלכי־צדק
in_hebrew.long_meaning: מלכי־צדק הוא שם המורכב משני שמות עבריים: מלך וצדק. הראשון מתייחס למלכותו ומעמדו הרם, והשני מתייחס לצדקתו וצדק האל. הוא מופיע במקרא כמלך שלמה, כוהן אל עליון, וקבלן הברית עם אברהם.

in_greek.name: Μελχισεδέκ
in_greek.long_meaning: Ο Μελχισεδέκ είναι όνομα που προέρχεται από την Εβραϊκή γλώσσα και σημαίνει 'Βασιλεύς της δικαιοσύνης' ή 'Βασιλεύς του Σαλήμ'. Στο Χριστιανισμό, ο Μελχισεδέκ αναφέρεται ως ο υψηλότερος ιερέας και βασιλιάς, που συναντάται στον Ψαλμό 110 και στην Επιστολή προς τους Εβραίους.

in_latin.name: Melchizedek
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Melchizedek derivatur ex Hebraeo et significat 'Rex justitiae' vel 'Rex Salem'. In Ecclesia Christiana, Melchizedek consideratur summus sacerdos et rex, cuius mysterium revelatur in Psalmo 110 et in Epistola ad Hebraeos.

in_english.name: Melchizedek
in_english.meaning: King of righteousness, King of Salem
in_english.long_meaning: The name Melchizedek originates from Hebrew, meaning 'King of righteousness' or 'King of Salem'. In Christianity, Melchizedek is a significant figure, representing a priest-king, mentioned in Psalm 110 and the Epistle to the Hebrews, symbolizing Jesus Christ's priestly and royal roles.

data.cultural_impact: Melchizedek's appearance in the Old Testament denotes his unique role as a priest-king, a combination of secular and spiritual power. He is regarded as a prefigurement of Jesus, who also held the dual roles of king and priest.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christian thought, Melchizedek serves as a typological figure and a reminder of the Messianic promise of Jesus, who would be both a priest and a king. His name represents the ideals of righteousness, priesthood, and kingship, which are intricately related to the identity of Jesus and the salvific mission of Christianity.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Melchizedek, meaning "king of righteousness," symbolizes the priest-king who offered an eternal priesthood through an unending sacrifice, foreshadowing Jesus as our eternal High Priest.

biblical_reference.note: High priest and king of Salem, encountered by Abraham

historical_references.reference: Melchizedek, a king of Salem and priest, met Abraham returning from the defeat of the kings and blessed him, receiving in turn a tithe of the spoils (Genesis 14:18-20).
historical_references.context: Melchizedek is mentioned for the first time in the Hebrew Bible, where he is described as a king of Salem and a priest who blesses Abraham and is in turn given a tithe of the spoils from Abraham's victory over the kings Chedorlaomer and his allies.

historical_references.reference: The New Testament Book of Hebrews refers to Melchizedek as a 'high priest forever' (Hebrews 7:3) and a 'king of righteousness' (Hebrews 7:2), whom it contrasts with the priests of the Levitical order and Aaron, who were mortal and required succession.
historical_references.time_period: Late Second Temple Period, approximately 50 CE
historical_references.context: The Epistle to the Hebrews, traditionally attributed to Paul, uses Melchizedek as an example in its argument that the priesthood of Jesus is superior to that of the Levitical priests. The author uses Melchizedek's name to illustrate the idea that a priest can be both king and priest, and that such a priest would not require succession because he is eternal.

modern_usage.modern_context: In the realm of Higher Education, Melchizedek is a subject of intense study in Religious Studies, particularly in the areas of Ancient Near Eastern Religions and Biblical Studies. On Academia.edu, scholars publish research papers exploring the meaning and significance of Melchizedek in the Hebrew Bible and Jewish tradition. In Religious Studies on Goodreads, books such as 'Melchizedek and His Priestly Descendants' and 'Melchizedek and the Sacred Bridge' are popular among those interested in the figure. On Wikipedia, Melchizedek is discussed as a priest-king from the Old Testament and a prefiguration of Jesus in Christian theology. Outside of academia, Melchizedek has gained popularity in Fantasy Literature, with references to him appearing in works such as 'The Kingkiller Chronicle' by Patrick Rothfuss and 'The Black Company' by Glen Cook.

name_in_real_life.story: Thomas Melchizedek from Rome, Italy embodies the meaning of Melchizedek - "King of Salem, priest of God Most High". Raised in a Christian family, they were taught to honor the significance of their name and walk in faith throughout their life.
